'''Harrison Bryce Jordan Barnes''' (born May 30, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] before being selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the first round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] with the seventh overall pick. Barnes won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the Warriors in [[2015 NBA Finals|2015]]. He also won a gold medal as a member of the [[2016 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2016 U.S. Olympic team]].

==High school career==
[[File:Harrison Barnes and Kyrie Irving at the 2010 Nike Hoop Summit.jpg|thumb|left|Barnes (right) with [[Kyrie Irving]] while playing for the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]]]]
Barnes was rated as the number one player in the class of 2010 by [[Scout.com]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2010 |title=Scout.com: Football Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref> and in the [[ESPNU]] 100.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/rankings |title=College Basketball Recruiting – ESPNU 100 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=August 24, 2010 |archive-date=February 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100214015945/http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2010&action=upsell&appRedirect=http%3A%2F%2Finsider.espn.go.com%2Fncb%2Frecruiting%2Ftracker%2Fespnu100%3F%26season%3D2010 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was rated as the number two player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals150 for class of 2010 |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |access-date=August 24, 2010 |archive-date=February 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100214145501/http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909 |url-status=dead }}</ref> As a junior, Barnes and teammate [[Doug McDermott]] led [[Ames High School]] to an Iowa 4A state championship where he had 24 points and eight rebounds in the final, capping off a 26–0 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dailycontributor.com/top-rated-basketball-recruit-harrison-barnes-chooses-north-carolina/8627/ |title=Top-Rated Basketball Recruit Harrison Barnes Chooses North Carolina |work=Daily Contributor |date=November 13, 2009 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref> As a senior, Barnes and McDermott led Ames to a 27–0 season and a second straight Iowa 4A state championship becoming Iowa's big-school class's first team to go undefeated in consecutive seasons. In the finals, he scored 19 points against [[Southeast Polk]]. He averaged 27.1 points, 10.4 rebounds, 4.0 steals, and 4.0 assists during his senior year and was selected to the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA First Team.<ref>{{cite news|last=Halley|first=Jim|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2010-all-usa-boys.htm|title=2010 All-USA boys basketball: Harrison Barnes leads the way|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 21, 2010 |access-date=September 11, 2011}}</ref> Barnes capped off his Ames High School career as their all-time leading scorer with 1,787 points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.timesrepublican.com/page/content.detail/id/523886.html?nav=5010 |title=Carolina-bound Barnes named Mr. Basketball |work=Times Republican |date=March 16, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307165451/http://www.timesrepublican.com/page/content.detail/id/523886.html?nav=5010 |archive-date=March 7, 2012 }}</ref> Barnes played in the fourth annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 Hoops Classic where he scored 18 points for Skip to My Lou.<ref>{{cite web |last=Calle |first=Franklyn |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/elite-24-recap-2/ |title=Elite 24 Recap |work=Slam Online |date=August 22, 2009 |access-date=August 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100710210644/http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/elite-24-recap-2/ |archive-date=July 10, 2010 }}</ref>

On January 20, 2010, it was announced that Barnes was selected to the 2010 Junior National Select Team. The team played at the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]], on April 10.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ceglinsky |first=Sean |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else/ |title=It's the USA Against Everyone Else |work=Slam Online |date=January 20, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref> He was also selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]] where he led the West team to a 107–104 victory. He scored a team high 18 points and was named co-MVP with [[Jared Sullinger]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/m2xSkj0QEd-lugAcxJTdpg/mcdonalds-all-american-night--knights-3-pointer-wins-it-for-the-west.htm |title=McDonald's All-American night: Knight's 3-pointer wins it for the West – MaxPreps News |publisher=Maxpreps.com |date=March 31, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref> He also played in the 2010 Jordan Brand Classic where he was named co-MVP with [[Kyrie Irving]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010jbc.html |title=Jordan Brand Classic |publisher=Nike.com |date=February 18, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100901111550/http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010jbc.html |archive-date=September 1, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 10, Barnes won the Morgan Wootten Player of the Year Award, which goes to the nation's top player.<ref>{{cite news|last=Halley |first=Jim |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2010-03-10-morgan-wootten-player-of-the-year_N.htm |title=Iowa's Harrison Barnes named Morgan Wootten Player of the Year |work=USA Today |date=March 10, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref>

Barnes completed nine [[advanced placement]] credits before graduating high school.<ref name=mercury>{{cite news|last=Brown |first=Daniel |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/warriors/ci_28135481/harrison-barnes-approval-ratings-through-roof |title=Harrison Barnes' Approval Rating Through the Roof |work=San Jose Mercury News |date=May 17, 2015 |access-date=May 21, 2015}}</ref>

===AAU===
Barnes played for All Iowa Attack and Howard Pulley Panthers (MN) on the AAU Circuit,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Harrison-Barnes-67225|title=Rivals.com|publisher=Yahoo!}}</ref> along with football prospect [[Seantrel Henderson]].<ref name="WinkeljohnESPN">{{Citation |last=Winkeljohn |first=Matt |date=November 12, 2009 |title=Harrison Barnes and Seantrel Henderson formed a one-two punch on the Twin Cities-based Pulley Panthers AAU team |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4647030 }}</ref>

Barnes considered offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4651146 |title=Barnes chooses Tar Heels |publisher=ESPN |date=November 13, 2009 |access-date=August 24, 2010}}</ref><ref name="scout1">{{cite web |url=http://northcarolina.scout.com/2/919368.html |title=Scout.com: Barnes to UNC |publisher=Northcarolina.scout.com |date=November 13, 2009 |access-date=August 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006062911/http://www.foxsportsnext.com/college/north-carolina-tar-heels.html |archive-date=October 6, 2012 }}</ref> He unofficially visited Kansas twice, for [[Midnight Madness (basketball)|Late Night in the Phog]] in October 2008 and a spring game against Tennessee.<ref>{{cite web |last=Temple |first=Jesse |date=May 4, 2009 |title=Pump N Run 'n' done |url=https://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/may/04/pump-n-run-n-done/ |access-date=June 19, 2025 |website=KUsports.com}}</ref> Barnes took official visits to North Carolina, Duke, Kansas, UCLA and Oklahoma, but he did not take an official visit to Iowa State since he lived only {{Convert|1|mi|km}} from campus, so Barnes chose to unofficially visit instead. On November 13, 2009, he [[Skype]]d coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] of North Carolina to announce his decision to join the Tar Heels.<ref name="scout1"/>

==College career==
[[File:Harrison Barnes cropped.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Barnes playing in the Carrier Classic game in November 2011]]

Barnes was seen as the potential first pick along with [[Jared Sullinger]], [[Kyrie Irving]] and [[Derrick Williams (basketball)|Derrick Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |date=2011-04-18 |title=Barnes' decision hints at larger shift |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/29861 |access-date=2022-02-15 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

Barnes' second season with the Tar Heels was also successful. He led the team in scoring 16 of their 38 games, helping the team to the ACC regular-season title, the final of the ACC tournament, and the Elite 8 of the NCAA tournament.

Barnes was the ninth player in school history to earn ACC Rookie of Year recognition and the fourth to do so under coach Roy Williams. Barnes scored the most points as a freshman in the ACC tournament since [[Phil Ford (basketball)|Phil Ford]] scored 78 points in 1975. In the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], he scored 84 points, the most points of any UNC freshman in history.

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2012–2016)===
====2012–13 season: All-Rookie honors====
[[File:Harrison Barnes warms up.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Barnes warming up as a rookie]]
On March 29, 2012, Barnes announced that he was entering the [[2012 NBA draft]] along with [[Tyler Zeller]], [[Kendall Marshall]] and [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]]. Barnes worked out with four teams: [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Washington Wizards]] and [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Wang |first=Gene |date=June 19, 2012 |title=Harrison Barnes works out for Wizards |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/harrison-barnes-works-out-for-wizards/2012/06/19/gJQAjIzGoV_blog.html |access-date=June 19, 2025 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> He was selected seventh overall by the [[Golden State Warriors]].

Warriors coach [[Mark Jackson]] said that Barnes was able to defend all five positions on the floor.<ref name="defense5">{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/video/channels/playoffs/2013/04/27/004120000163-den-gsw-postgame-jackson-game3.nba/index.html | title=Press Pass: Mark Jackson | publisher=National Basketball Association | date=April 27, 2013 | access-date=April 27, 2013}}</ref> In Game 4 of the semifinals of the [[2013 NBA Playoffs]] on May 12, Barnes scored 26 points and added 10 rebounds.<ref name="2013 1RND G2">{{cite web |author=Lepper, Geoff |date=May 12, 2013 |title=Notebook: Warriors 97, Spurs 87 |url=http://www.nba.com/data/html/nbacom/gameinfo/20130512/0041200234_notebook.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602031845/http://www.nba.com/data/html/nbacom/gameinfo/20130512/0041200234_notebook.html |archive-date=June 2, 2015 |access-date=May 12, 2013 |publisher=NBA}}</ref> Two days later, the NBA named him to the 2012–13 All-Rookie first team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/14/all-rookie-team-official-release/index.html|title=Lillard headlines 2012–13 All-Rookie Team|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=May 14, 2013|access-date=May 14, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607122121/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/14/all-rookie-team-official-release/index.html|archive-date=June 7, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barnes also placed sixth in [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting, in a tie with [[Chris Copeland]] (eight points total).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/|title=Portland's Lillard named 2012–13 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=July 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118231137/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/05/01/kia-rookie-of-the-year-lillard/|archive-date=January 18, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2013–14 season: Sixth man====
With the arrival of [[Andre Iguodala]], Barnes became a reserve player. He again participated in BBVA Compass [[Rising Stars Challenge]]. He was chosen as a starter for Team Hill.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/01/29/rising-stars-roster/|title=Lillard, Carter-Williams headline 2014 Rising Stars Challenge|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 29, 2014|access-date=April 17, 2014}}</ref> Barnes finished the game with 16 points, three rebounds, three assists, and two steals in 23 minutes in the team's win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140214/HILWEB/gameinfo.html|title=Team Hill at Team Webber|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 14, 2014|access-date=April 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140215042015/http://www.nba.com/games/20140214/HILWEB/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 15, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 16, 2014, he scored a career-high 30 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the final regular season game for the Warriors. The Warriors finished the regular season with a 51–31 record, going into the playoffs as the #6-seed in the West, but went on to lose to the [[2013–14 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] in seven games during the first round.

====2014–15 season: Championship season====
Under new head coach [[Steve Kerr]], Barnes moved back into the starting lineup and had an immediate impact. On March 18, 2015, he scored a season-high 25 points in a 114–95 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ATLGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks at Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 3, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925183132/http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ATLGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 2, he hit a running shot in the lane with less than a second remaining, lifting the Warriors to a narrow 107–106 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref name="mercury"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150402/PHXGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Suns at Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 3, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003203936/http://www.nba.com/games/20150402/PHXGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 3, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the playoffs, Barnes had a quiet breakout performance in the semifinals against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He averaged 12.8 points per game, while shooting 54.4% from the field, a performance lauded by many basketball insiders due to the reputation of the Grizzlies' defense.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://grantland.com/the-triangle/2015-nba-playoffs-golden-state-warriors-harrison-barnes-improvement/|title=Bay Area Bellwether: How the Improvement of Harrison Barnes Mirrors Golden State's Ascent|first=Kirk|last=Goldsberry|date=May 21, 2015}}</ref> In Games 4, 5, and 6, Barnes made several key plays in clutch situations. When the Warriors were losing by double digits in the first quarter of Game 5, Barnes got the comeback started with several key shots, which turned into a rout once teammate Stephen Curry was able to shoulder much of the load. On May 27, in the Warriors' Western Conference Finals clinching Game 5 victory, Barnes scored 24 points to help lead them to the [[NBA Finals]] for the first time in 40 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150527/HOUGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets at Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=May 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529180626/http://www.nba.com/games/20150527/HOUGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=May 29, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barnes won his first NBA championship with the Warriors after they defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the [[2015 NBA Finals]] in six games.

====2015–16 season: NBA record for wins====
[[File:Harrison Barnes with Warriors 2016.jpg|thumb|upright|Barnes in his final season with the Warriors]]
Barnes helped the Warriors go 17–0 to start the season before a sprained left ankle ruled him out for 16 straight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/barneha02/gamelog/2016/|title=Harrison Barnes 2015-16 Game Log - Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> Barnes returned to action on January 4 against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], scoring eight points off the bench in a 111–101 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/CHAGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Hornets vs Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170127233556/http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/CHAGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 27, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 7, Barnes scored 21 points against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], scoring in double figures for a ninth straight game, a career high. The win made the Warriors the second team in NBA history to win 70 games in a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160407/SASGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Spurs vs Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408072344/http://www.nba.com/games/20160407/SASGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 8, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Warriors went on to win an NBA record 73 games, eclipsing the 72–10 record set by the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]].

Through the first two rounds of the playoffs, Barnes shot just 36% from the field. In the Western Conference Finals against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], he shot 48% from the field while averaging 8.7 points per game to help the Warriors defeat the Thunder in seven games after overcoming a 3–1 deficit to advance to the [[2016 NBA Finals]]. In Game 1 of the NBA Finals against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Barnes had a 13-point performance to help the Warriors win 104–89.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160602/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603100145/http://www.nba.com/games/20160602/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2016-06-03|title=Cavaliers vs Warriors|website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref> Despite the Warriors going up 3–1 in the series following a Game 4 win, they went on to lose the series in seven games to become the first team in NBA history to lose the championship series after being up 3–1. Barnes only shot 16% in the last three games.

===Dallas Mavericks (2016–2019)===
====2016–17 season====
On July 9, 2016, Barnes signed a four-year, $94 million contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ahmadi |first=Arya |date=July 9, 2016 |title=Mavericks sign forward Harrison Barnes |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-forward-harrison-barnes/ |access-date=June 19, 2025 |work=mavs.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=July 6, 2016 |title=Done deal: SF Harrison Barnes signs four-year, $94 million deal with Mavericks |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2016/07/07/done-deal-sf-harrison-barnes-signs-four-year-94-million-deal-with-mavericks/ |access-date=June 19, 2025 |work=The Dallas Morning News}}</ref> He made his Mavericks debut in their season opener on October 26, recording 19 points and nine rebounds in a 130–121 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899379|title=Turner's opening act leads Pacers past Mavs, 130–121 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, Barnes scored a career-high 31 points in a 106–98 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899457|title=Rockets top Mavs 106–98 with Nowitzki out for home opener|publisher=ESPN|date=October 28, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> He bested that mark on November 6, scoring 34 points in an 86–75 overtime win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899540|title=Barnes scores career-high 34, Mavs beat Bucks 86–75 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}}</ref> Barnes scored 30 points or more seven times during the 2016–17 season, including five 31-point games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/barneha02/gamelog/2017/|title=Harrison Barnes 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 22, 2018}}</ref> After never finishing better than fourth in scoring in his four seasons with the Golden State Warriors, Barnes led the Mavericks with a career-best 19.2 points per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2016–17 Dallas Mavericks Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/DAL/2017.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=25 August 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
Barnes would again lead the Mavericks in scoring in 2017–2018, though the team finished 24–58 and 13th of 15 teams in the Western Conference.<ref>{{cite web |title=2017–18 Dallas Mavericks Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/DAL/2018.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=25 August 2019 |language=en}}</ref> On November 7, 2017, Barnes scored a season-high 31 points against the [[Washington Wizards]]. He tied that mark on November 20 against the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/barneha02/gamelog/2018/|title=Harrison Barnes 2017–18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 22, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, Barnes banked a 30-footer as the horn sounded to lift the Mavericks to a 95–94 victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Barnes led the Mavericks with 22 points, nine of them coming in the fourth quarter to help Dallas thwart a late Memphis comeback.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975011|title=Barnes' 30-footer at the horn lifts Mavs over Grizzlies|publisher=ESPN|date=November 22, 2017|access-date=November 22, 2017}}</ref> On December 26, 2017, he tied his career high with his sixth double-double of the season after registering 16 points and 10 rebounds in a 98–93 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He previously achieved it in Golden State's championship season of 2014–15.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975245|title=Barea, Mavs end another Raptors 6-game streak with 98–93 win|publisher=ESPN|date=December 26, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> On January 10, 2018, he had 13 of his 25 points in the fourth quarter of the Mavericks' 115–111 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He made all five of his shots in the fourth quarter and added 11 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975349|title=Barnes, Ferrell lead Mavericks past Hornets 115–111|publisher=ESPN|date=January 10, 2018|access-date=January 10, 2018}}</ref> He finished the season with eight double-doubles, setting a new personal best.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.nba.com/player/203084/?sort=DD2&dir=1|title=Harrison Barnes advanced stats|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=May 29, 2018}}</ref>

====2018–19 season====
Barnes missed the first four games of the 2018–19 season because of a strained right hamstring.<ref name=season-debut>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070750|title=Lowry has 20 as Raptors win 6th straight, beat Mavs 116–107|publisher=ESPN|date=October 26, 2018|access-date=October 27, 2018}}</ref> In his season debut on October 26, he shot 5 for 17 and scored 14 points in a 116–107 loss to the Raptors.<ref name="season-debut"/> On December 2, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 114–110 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071022|title=Barnes, Jordan star in Mavericks' 114–110 win over Clippers|publisher=ESPN|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref> On December 31, he scored 25 points and matched his career high with seven 3-pointers in nine attempts in a 122–102 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071223|title=Westbrook rebounds with triple-double as Thunder beat Mavs|publisher=ESPN|date=December 31, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2019–2024)===
On February 6, 2019, while in the middle of a game for Dallas against the [[Charlotte Hornets]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071480|title=Mavericks top Hornets 99–93 as Dallas deals Barnes to Kings|publisher=ESPN|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 7, 2019}}</ref> Barnes was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Zach Randolph]] and [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Khan |first=Shahbaz |date=February 6, 2019 |title=Kings Acquire Forward Harrison Barnes |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-acquire-forward-harrison-barnes |access-date=February 7, 2019 |publisher=NBA}}</ref> He made his debut for the Kings two days later, scoring 12 points in a 102–96 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071497|title=Kings come back from 11 down in fourth to beat Heat 102–96|publisher=ESPN|date=February 8, 2019|access-date=February 8, 2019}}</ref> Barnes signed a four-year, $85 million contract extension with the [[Sacramento Kings]] following the 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ham |first=James |date=June 30, 2019 |title=Source: Harrison Barnes, Kings agree to four-year, $85M contract |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/source-harrison-barnes-kings-agree-four-year-85m-contract |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=RSN |language=en}}</ref>

On October 20, 2021, Barnes scored a game-leading 36 points, including a career-high eight three-point shots, during a 124–121 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-21 |title=Barnes Has 36 And the Kings Spoil Portland's Opener 124-121 |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-10-21/barnes-has-36-and-the-kings-spoil-portland-s-opener-124-121 |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=bloomberg.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On October 27, Barnes hit a game-winning fadeaway three pointer to secure victory for the Kings against the [[Phoenix Suns]], 110–107.

On November 20, 2022, Barnes scored 27 points and grabbed nine rebounds during a 137–129 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salerno |first=Cameron |date=2022-11-20 |title=6 game streak: Kings beat Pistons 137-129 |url=https://www.abc10.com/article/sports/kings-beat-pistons-137-129/103-bce5e91f-2a64-487d-abf8-bd9e9fe55088 |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=abc10.com |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On June 29, 2023, Barnes signed a three-year, $54 million extension through the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |date=June 29, 2023 |title=Harrison Barnes staying with Kings on 3-year, $54M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37936721/harrison-barnes-staying-kings-3-year-54m-extension |access-date=June 25, 2026 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2024–present)===
On July 8, 2024, Barnes was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade, which also included the [[Sacramento Kings]] and the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Acquire Harrison Barnes|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-acquire-harrison-barnes|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 8, 2024}}</ref> Barnes started all 82 games for San Antonio during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 12.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.7 assists.<ref>{{cite web | last=O'Donnell | first=Ricky | title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul | website=SB Nation | date=2025-04-14 | url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>

On June 29, 2026, Barnes re-signed with the Spurs on a one-year, $8 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reports: Harrison Barnes will re-sign with San Antonio|url=https://www.nba.com/news/harrison-barnes-will-re-sign-with-san-antonio|access-date=June 30, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en|date=June 30, 2026|last=|first=}}</ref>

==National team career==
In June 2016, Barnes was named in the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] for the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-06-25 |title=Report: Ames native Harrison Barnes named to Team USA |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/basketball/2016/06/25/harrison-barnes-team-usa-rio-de-janeiro-olympic-games/86386554/ |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=[[USA Today]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He helped Team USA win the gold medal in Rio, and in four games, Barnes averaged 4.3 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/barnes-harrison.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150810122652/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/barnes-harrison.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 10, 2015|title=Harrison Barnes}}</ref>

In August 2019, Barnes was named as part of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] for the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]]. He helped team USA to a 6–2 record and a seventh-place finish in the tournament, losing in the quarterfinal round to France and in the fifth-place game to Serbia before rallying to win the seventh-place game against Poland. Barnes averaged 11.6 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.

Barnes is a [[Christians|Christian]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Zogg |first=Michael |date=December 10, 2009 |title=BASKETBALL: Faith guides phenom |url=http://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/article_5a0ecef6-d60c-5a76-a7bc-4e54baaac342.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022123451/https://www.iowastatedaily.com/sports/article_5a0ecef6-d60c-5a76-a7bc-4e54baaac342.html |archive-date=October 22, 2021 |access-date=May 31, 2016 |work=[[Iowa State Daily]]}}</ref> He is also a [[teetotaler]]; he had his first sip of alcohol after winning the [[2015 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Extra Mustard |date=June 17, 2015 |title=Harrison Barnes's first sip of alcohol was Warriors' victory champagne |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2015/06/17/nba-finals-warriors-harrison-barnes-champagne-alcohol |access-date=June 19, 2025 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> On July 29, 2017, he married Brittany Johnson at Rosecliff in Newport, Rhode Island.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pearson |first=Zack |date=July 29, 2017 |title=UNC in NBA: Harrison Barnes gets married over weekend |url=https://keepingitheel.com/2017/07/30/unc-nba-harrison-barnes-gets-married-weekend/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730224916/https://keepingitheel.com/2017/07/30/unc-nba-harrison-barnes-gets-married-weekend/ |archive-date=July 30, 2017 |access-date=July 30, 2017 |work=Fansided}}</ref>

On September 15, 2022, Barnes' high school alma mater honored him for his career and community support by naming the gymnasium and basketball court at the new high school after him and electing him to the school's Hall of Fame.<ref>{{cite web |last=Randleman |first=Joe |date=September 16, 2022 |title=Harrison Barnes humbled by Ames High gym dedication: NBA star enters school's Hall of Fame |url=https://www.amestrib.com/story/sports/2022/09/16/nba-star-harrison-barnes-new-ames-high-school-gym-dedication/10388498002/ |access-date=September 19, 2022 |work=Ames Tribune}}</ref>
